If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

content.text:
I re-graded both files without running anything. Bash was denied, so I couldn't probe the startup error paths or run `npm test`. All six requested fixes are in place, and I found nothing that goes against the spec. Verdict: pass, 9/10.

**The six fixes from last round**
- **Test script**: `package.json:9` is `node --test "test/**/*.test.mjs"`, which matches the Node 22 note. There is no `test/` folder yet, so `npm test` has nothing to run until the testing section adds it.
- **PORT error**: `server.mjs:349` passes the value through `JSON.stringify`, so stray control characters can't break it into more than one line. It exits with code 1 via `fail`.
- **Atomic save**: `server.mjs:133-142` writes a temp file beside the data file, renames it over, removes the temp on failure and rethrows. `commit` (239-243) only updates memory after the save succeeds, so a failed save changes nothing, the next id included. It creates no folders.
- **Logging unexpected errors**: `logUnexpected` (298-301) squashes whitespace into a single stderr line. Expected (`HttpError`) failures are not logged, and the only stdout write is line 362.
- **Splitting createApp**: `route` is now a top-level function (265-286). `createApp` is about 43 lines and every function is under 50. The file is 366 lines.
- **clientError cleanup**: line 357 ends the socket only if it is still writable and destroys it otherwise.
- **DELETE id guard**: line 232 needs both `ID_PATTERN` and `Number.isSafeInteger`, so a huge id that rounds to an existing one gives 404.

**Spec check (no regressions)**
- **Startup**: the order is PORT, then the data file, then listen. ENOENT means no bookings yet. Any other read error, bad JSON or wrong layout prints `cannot read data file <DATA_FILE as given>`. A relative `DATA_FILE` is resolved against the working directory. A port that can't be bound reports its `err.code`.
- **Booking rules**: they run in spec order, 415 then 413 then 400 then 409. The 413 check counts every byte received while keeping at most 10001 in memory. The byte order mark is kept because the body is decoded with `Buffer#toString`. The title is trimmed with `trim`. The 409 names the earliest-starting overlapping booking.
- **Routing**: paths are compared byte for byte. `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/` are 404, `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405, and HEAD and OPTIONS get 405. A 204 has no body or Content-Type. Bookings are sorted by date, start, then room order, and the date filter uses `has` and `get`. Requests run through one queue that never rejects, so overlapping requests behave as if handled one at a time.

**Minor issues (none blocking)**
- Two empty catch handlers swallow errors silently (lines 139 and 318). Both have comments explaining why, so this is acceptable, but a stderr line on 139 would be easy to add.
- The server `error` handler (line 360) stays attached after startup, so any later server error would print "cannot listen" and exit.
- `readBody` uses the deprecated `aborted` event (line 161).
- `isValidTitle` trims twice (line 72), and `HttpError` doesn't set its `name`.

## GRADE
Overall: 9/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 9 — clear sections; route, servePage, writeResult and writeFailure are separate; state is frozen and replaced, never changed in place
naming: 9 — descriptive and consistent (loadState, saveState, commit, splitTarget, requireMethod); HttpError lacks a `name`
duplication: 9 — shared validators and `overlaps` are used by both the API and the data-file check; only the double trim on line 72 is repeated
size: 9 — 366-line file, all functions under 50 lines (createApp about 43)
errors: 8 — startup errors are one line with exit code 1, listen errors use err.code, unexpected request errors give 500 and one stderr line, a failed save leaves state unchanged; two commented empty catches and a listen-error handler that outlives startup
tests: n/a — written by the testing section
security: 9 — no secrets, page paths come from a fixed whitelist, input checked at the boundary, body memory capped
leftovers: 10 — no console.log, debug code, commented-out code or TODOs
Fixes:
- /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/server.mjs:360 use `server.once('error', …)` before listening, or remove it in the listen callback, so a later server error isn't reported as "cannot listen" and doesn't exit the process
- /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/server.mjs:139 write one stderr line when removing the temp file fails, instead of `.catch(() => {})`
- /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/server.mjs:161 replace the deprecated `aborted` event with `req.on('close', …)` and check `!req.complete`
- /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/server.mjs:72 trim once into a local and check its length
- /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/server.mjs:44 set `this.name = 'HttpError'` in the constructor
